extraction.name: MathVista
extraction.description: MathVista is a benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples, derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). The benchmark covers seven mathematical reasoning types (algebraic, arithmetic, geometry, logical, numeric common sense, scientific, statistical) and five primary tasks (figure QA, geometry problem solving, math word problem, textbook QA, visual QA), encompassing diverse visual contexts including natural images, geometry diagrams, abstract scenes, synthetic scenes, charts, plots, tables, function plots, and puzzle test figures.
extraction.creator: UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research Redmond
extraction.inLanguage: English (93.43%), with 6.57% non-English including Chinese and Persian
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MathVista was collected through three main processes: (1) Collection of 9 MathQA datasets in multimodal settings (up to 400 examples each, totaling 2,666 examples); (2) Review of more than 70 VQA datasets, selecting 19 publicly available ones containing math-related instances, using heuristic rules to automatically select examples with numeric answers or quantity words, followed by manual labeling by three expert annotators (2,739 examples after majority voting); (3) Creation of three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) with 736 newly curated examples manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations. Due to heterogeneity of sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source data drawn from 31 source datasets: 19 existing VQA datasets, 9 existing MathQA datasets, and 3 newly annotated datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA). IQTest sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms; PaperQA sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface (https://huggingface.co/papers); FunctionQA covers functional plots with algebraic reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: PaperQA sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning (examples with numeric answers or containing quantity words from a predefined dictionary). False positives were manually filtered. Dataset split into testmini (1,000 examples) and test (5,141 examples) using a sampling strategy: first randomly sample with a threshold of 4 per source dataset, then sample remaining questions proportionally. KL Divergence between testmini and entire set: 0.008; Total Variation distance: 0.035.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three expert annotators manually labeled VQA examples to determine mathematical reasoning involvement using a GUI tool with detailed instructions. Annotators were trained with positive/negative examples and given three labeling options (Yes/No/Unsure). For the three new datasets, questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields, with each dataset independently annotated by three reviewers (inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2%; only 6 of 736 questions had disagreements, resolved through team discussion). Metadata (question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, visual context) was annotated. Mathematical reasoning category labels were verified by expert annotators on 1,000 examples; 94.1% had exact same set of reasoning types between automatic and human annotations, with 98.79% individual labels identical.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom GUI annotation tool developed by authors (shown in Figures 22, 23, 24). Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) was used for human performance baseline and Multimodal Bard assessment.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement analysis using Fleiss Kappa score yielded 0.775, indicating substantial consistency. For new datasets, inter-annotation consistency rate was 99.2%. Disagreements resolved through discussion among the review team. For mathematical reasoning labels, 94.1% of examples had exact same set of reasoning types from automatic and human annotations; 98.79% individual labels were identical.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 annotators per item for VQA math reasoning labeling and new dataset annotation
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Expert annotators (three for VQA labeling); graduate students in STEM fields for new dataset annotation. Human performance baseline annotators from Amazon Mechanical Turk with satisfactory annotating history (>5,000 HIT tasks, acceptance score >0.99, and high school diploma or higher).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: EasyOCR (for OCR text detection); Multimodal Bard (for image caption generation); GPT-4 (for answer extraction with >99.5% accuracy based on 200 example preliminary study)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Dataset divided into testmini (1,000 examples) for model development validation and test (5,141 examples) for standard evaluation. Answer labels for test will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination. An online evaluation platform will be maintained. Authors committed to ongoing maintenance, refining data noise based on community feedback, and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Dataset may include images of people (e.g., celebrities for age gap questions), though Multimodal Bard restricts responses to images of people. Language attribute is annotated (English 93.43%, non-English including Chinese and Persian 6.57%).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark plays a critical role in the development of general-purpose AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks, with applications in educational disciplines, helping analysts with logical queries about statistical data, and assisting in theorem proving and scientific discovery.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Dataset coverage limitations: may have gaps in certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. Focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts spanning specific domains like science and college-level math necessitates more labor-intensive data collection. Scalability and generalizability to other domains remain a concern. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations. Annotations lack unified format and structure due to heterogeneity of sources. Study focused exclusively on most recent and prominent models given the rapid development in foundation models.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and Validation: testmini subset (1,000 examples) intended for model development validation or for those with limited computing resources; test subset (5,141 examples) for standard evaluation. Used to benchmark mathematical reasoning capabilities of LLMs and LMMs in visual contexts. Evaluation protocols include response generation, answer extraction, and score calculation using accuracy metrics.
